Binary search works by repeatedly dividing the search interval in half.  
To decide which half to continue with, the algorithm compares the target value with the middle element of the current interval.  
If the data were not sorted, there is no guarantee that elements to the left of a given value are all smaller or all larger than it, so the comparison would not give reliable information about where the target could still be found.  
Only when the collection is **sorted** does this invariant hold:

*All elements to the left of a given index are ≤ the element at that index,*
*all elements to the right are ≥ that element.*

Thus each comparison eliminates roughly half of the remaining possibilities, leading to the logarithmic O(log n) time complexity.
